metadata.scenario: A caregiver at a patient's home calls saying the patient is having difficulty breathing with oxygen saturation at 88. She asks if a nurse can come immediately. The receptionist tells her to call 911 first and dispatches a nurse. Tense, urgent call.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Dorothy Henderson. I need help urgently. Oh no, Dorothy! What's going on? A caregiver at my home just called. I'm having difficulty breathing, and my oxygen saturation is at 88. That sounds serious. Has the caregiver called 911? No, not yet. Should they do that? Yes, absolutely. Please have them call 911 right away. Okay, I'll tell them. Can we get a nurse to come immediately? We will dispatch a nurse right now, but please ensure 911 is called first. Yes, they are calling now. I’m really worried! I understand, Dorothy. Stay calm. We're sending a nurse from our team urgently. Thank you. Can you tell me who will be coming? It will be Robert Davis, our Registered Nurse. He specializes in Cardiac Care and will be there shortly. Good. I just want to make sure I'm okay. You're going to be alright. Is there anything else your caregiver needs while waiting? Just some reassurance that help is on the way. I’ll make sure they know to stay by your side until Robert arrives. Thank you. I really appreciate it. You're welcome, Dorothy. Please keep me updated. After this, we’ll need a follow-up on your care plan. Yes, I’ll need that. And if you need more frequent nurse visits after this, we can arrange that too. That sounds good. Great! I’ll check in with you later. Stay strong, help is on the way. Thanks, Margaret. I’ll do my best.
